fixes.explanation: Oh, friend, it's TRUE, and it's sitting right there in the prayer. Elijah says, "Answer me, O LORD! Answer me, so that this people will know that You, the LORD, are God, and that You have turned their hearts back again." (1 Kings 18:37) He asks twice, plain and bold, like a man who isn't mumbling. And he says why: so the people will know.

Another sacrifice? Friend, the altar had its big moment already. Elijah says, “Go and tell Ahab, ‘Prepare your chariot and go down before the rain stops you.’…” (1 Kings 18:44) Ahab is the king of Israel. This message is all chariot and rain, no second round at the altar.

Bethel? Nice guess, friend, but Ahab isn't pointing his chariot there. The text says, "So Ahab rode away and went to Jezreel." (1 Kings 18:45) The sky is dark with clouds and wind, and heavy rain is falling. Bethel never even makes it into the verse, so it can't take the credit.
